kind: structural study of the 2D a-region after b-elimination (nominal rings fixed)
S1_variables: a=(x,y) in K_A (convex ring-only disk intersection); the only non-constant radicals are k_i(a)=sqrt(r^2-|a-c_i|^2/4), i=0,4; with s_i=|a-c_i| the relations are k_i^2=r^2-s_i^2/4, s_i^2=|a-c_i|^2, s_i>0
S2_q_form: q_i(a) = (a+c_i)/2 + k_i * perp(c_i-a)/|c_i-a|; branch = side of the reference b-point (orientation preserved; the C894-retracted half-plane direction is NOT used)
S4_rationalisation: a2=L0/s0, b2=L1/s1, c2=L01/(s0 s1), X=Xc/(s0 s1), all s_i>0. Then max(a2,b2,c2)>4r^2 <=> max(L0 s1, L1 s0, L01) > 4 r^2 s0 s1 (degree <=4); the acuteness comparisons multiply the same way; the acute-product clause a2 b2 c2 > 4 r^2 X^2 becomes L0 L1 L01 > 4 r^2 Xc^2 (degree <=10). So every a-condition is POLYNOMIAL in (x,y,k0,k1,s0,s1) after clearing positive denominators, subject to two quadratic relations: quantifier elimination exists in principle, at the price of a 1-dimensional boundary (see [E]).
S5_domain_and_degeneracies: domain: a in K_A = B(0,1-r) cap cap_{j in {4..8}} B(p_j,r) (convex) with k_i >= 0 and the branch side sign det(c_i-a, b_ref-a) != 0

k_i = 0 <=> |a-c_i| = 2r: the two circle branches coalesce; the rho-argument does NOT exclude this boundary (rho >= r does not contradict rho <= r) -- such tuples are excluded by the STRICT G bound instead (q_near = q_far = m)
s_i = 0 <=> a = c_i: central face triangle degenerates (circumradius undefined)
branch failure: det(c_i-a, b_ref-a) = 0 (a collinear with c_i and b_ref)
loss region: the single-disk clause is EXACT only where K_B misses the distal disk (a certified (H2) box); outside it the clause set changes
the clauses contain crescent-type "exactly one of two disks" parts, which are curved (see [E]): no finite POINT candidate set decides the region

E_exact_convexity_counterexample.data: r=1, A=(-3/5,0), C=(3/5,0); the two radius-1 circle centres through A,C are q=(0,4/5), q'=(0,-4/5): |q-A|=|q-C|=|q'-A|=|q'-C|=1 exactly
E_exact_convexity_counterexample.verdict: q and q' are crescent points ((g_plus,g_minus)=(-1,39/25) resp. (39/25,-1)); their midpoint (0,0) has both g=-9/25<0, i.e. lies in the OPEN lens which the crescent excludes.  Crescent is NOT convex -- exactly, rational data.
E_exact_convexity_counterexample.consequence: clauses of this shape appear verbatim in the b-fiber relaxation (H1-H6: 'in exactly one of two disks', two moving disks disjoint, min-norm vs the open norm ball). Hence the a-region is a Boolean combination of CURVED pieces: the boundary is 1-dimensional; no finite set of POINT candidates decides it (3-element witnesses alone cannot make `a` finite).
